players.name: Josh Allen
notes: The Keep #1 · average 1.6 across 10 Superflex boards
The Board #1 on the long proprietary aggregate
Redraft PPR #27 (Yates 28, FantasyPros 26)
Redraft Standard #27
plus: Seven-board Superflex lock: Keep #1, average 2.0.
Dual-threat floor still separates him from every other aging QB1.
minus: Turns 31 in 2026 — first real dynasty age tax on a perennial 1.01.
Yates PPR has him in the late 20s; 1QB redraft does not pay the SF premium.
grafs: Josh Allen is still the player Ball Keep is built around. Seven sources — PFN, Dynasty Nerds, FantasyPros, KeepTradeCut, and the three X experts we track — all have him inside the top four Superflex assets, and the average lands at 2.0. That is not a recency spike. It is the market admitting that a quarterback who runs, extends, and finishes in the end zone is the safest way to keep a Superflex roster relevant through 2029.

The 2025 tape is the same argument on film: launch-point throws and designed keepers, with the Bills still built to let him create when protection breaks. Redraft boards (Field Yates has him in the high 20s) treat him as a mid QB1 because 1QB leagues do not have to pay the second-starter tax. Dynasty Superflex does. That split is the whole point of The Keep.

The minus is honest: he will be 31 this season, and the first time a 23-year-old passer (Maye) outranks him on a short list, the age conversation gets louder. We are not selling the 1.01 for that. We are naming it. If you are rebuilding past 2028, Maye is the bet. If you are trying to win the next two title windows, Allen is still the chip you do not put in a trade calculator for fun.

grafs: Drake Maye is the dynasty argument of 2026. Three of our short expert lists (FantasyPros ECR, Andrew Erickson, Pat Fitzmaurice) rank him the Superflex 1.01, Derek Brown has him second, and the long boards (PFN, Dynasty Nerds) park him third behind only Allen. The Keep average is 2.43. That is a 23-year-old passer being priced like a finished product.

The 2025 film is why. The Can't-Miss clip we embedded is the AFC run in miniature: Maye dropping a touchdown and a receiver finishing like a superhero. New England's offense finally looks like a place where a long-striding quarterback can push the ball and scramble without the supporting cast being a weekly apology. Superflex managers who waited on the 2024 draft capital got paid.

The pushback is KeepTradeCut at six and redraft boards that still treat him as a high-end QB2 in 1QB. That is useful. It means you can still find a manager who thinks Allen/Lamar/Hurts are 'safer' and will overpay in picks to move down. Ball Keep's stance: the experts have moved. The startup ADP will follow. Do not be the last one holding the 2024 'he might be Caleb-tier' take.

The honest minus is architecture. Atlanta can become a game-script problem, and Superflex drafters who believe Maye/Allen/Chase are less replaceable will let Bijan slide one spot. If you are in 1QB or a redraft league that rewards rushing volume, do not overthink it. He is a first-round pick with a younger age curve than CMC, Henry, or Barkley.

Day 3 / 3rd-round dart
plus: Rookie #20 — Day 3 / third-round dart, Penn State mate of Singleton, Commanders 23-carry debut clip.
Washington can feed a rookie back if the veterans slip; the preseason volume was a tell.
minus: Day-3 RBs are committees until proven otherwise.
Commanders' passing game (Daniels) can steal scoring; this is a stash, not a starter.
grafs: Kaytron Allen is the last name on our 2026 rookie sheet: Day 3 dart, Penn State bruiser, Commanders preseason 23-carry debut. That 23-carry clip is the plus — someone in Washington wanted to see him as a hammer. The minus is that preseason hammers become September inactives every year.
If the Commanders' backfield opens, Allen is a waiver-wire hero in redraft and a nice taxi hit in dynasty. If it doesn't, he was Rookie 20 and you spent a third. Superflex thirds are for this.
Do not draft him before Singleton unless you are in love. Do draft him at the end of a rookie draft if you like mean runners. We like mean runners. We like them cheaper.

The Board #202 on the long proprietary aggregate
Volatile SF 2nd/3rd · high STD DEV
plus: Rookie #19 — Cardinals QB dart, 2025 CFP Cotton Bowl vs. Ohio State reel, volatile Superflex 2nd/3rd.
High-variance passers can still hit in 2QB; the arm talent is on the clip.
minus: Our note: high STD DEV. This is a dart, not a plan.
Arizona already has a roster; year-one starting is not the base case.
grafs: Carson Beck is the volatile Superflex dart we put 19th on the rookie board with the words high standard deviation. The 2025 Cotton Bowl reel against Ohio State is a quarterback in a big environment. Arizona taking a swing is how 2QB leagues stay interesting and how 1QB leagues stay away.

If Beck sits, you waited. If Beck plays and it works, you look like a genius at 2.08. If Beck plays and it doesn't, you took a QB instead of Stowers. Superflex can take that bet once. It should not take it twice.
Rank him as a third QB on a Superflex roster, not as Mendoza insurance you paid a first for. The clip is fun. The rank is a warning dressed as a compliment.

bb_waivers_dynasty.why: Young Red Sox arm. Stash, do not stream.

bb_waivers_redraft.why: Twins saves. Not a committee you ignore in September.

bb_waivers_redraft.name: Cam Schlittler
bb_waivers_redraft.why: Best two-start / rest-of-season streaming ace who is not locked everywhere.

bb_waivers_redraft.name: Drew Rasmussen
bb_waivers_redraft.why: Rays innings. Stream him until he proves you shouldn't.

bb_waivers_redraft.name: Parker Messick
bb_waivers_redraft.why: September starter you can stream twice. Ratios over wins.

bb_waivers_redraft.why: Mets arm with enough Ks to start in a 12-team this week.

bb_waivers_redraft.why: If he is healthy and free, he is not a stream, he is a roster.
